question: A man goes to Nagpur from Visakhapatnam at a speed of 24 km/hr and returns to Visakhapatnam at speed of 40 km/hr, through the same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the same distance is traveled in both directions, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 24 × 40) ÷ (24 + 40)

⇒ Average Speed = 1920 ÷ 64

⇒ Average Speed = 30 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Visakhapatnam to Nagpur (S₁) = 24 km/hr

Speed from Nagpur to Visakhapatnam (S₂) = 40 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculation:**

Let the assumed distance between the two cities be the LCM of given speeds (24 and 40).

⇒ Assumed Distance D = LCM(24, 40) = 120 km

⇒ Time taken for onward journey = 120 ÷ 24 = 5 hrs

⇒ Time taken for return journey = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 hrs

⇒ Total distance covered = 120 + 120 = 240 km

⇒ Total time taken = 5 + 3 = 8 hrs

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 240 ÷ 8 = 30 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

When different distances d₁, d₂, d₃... are covered at speeds s₁, s₂, s₃..., Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time) = (d₁ + d₂ + d₃...) ÷ (d₁/s₁ + d₂/s₂ + d₃/s₃...)

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If three equal distances are covered at speeds x, y and z, Average Speed = 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx)

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, Relative Speed = s₁ + s₂. When moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = |s₁ − s₂|.
